Crew rest and the working day
The rest a flyer needs before his day starts. The crew-rest warning and the tight crew-rest advisory move with it.
Days in a row
A day on the programme beyond this many in a row raises the red break-day warning.
A longer day, first commitment to last, shows the grey long-day note.

With no in-time or rally typed, a flyer's day starts here: his long day, OIL and Insights hours count from it. It also sets when the tight crew-rest advisory shows. "+ In-time / Rally" fills in take-off less this time.
Sets the suggested B on a line with no brief typed, and a blank B is checked against it. With no in-time typed, crew rest counts to this B. A published day keeps its B until it is published again.
A man counts as busy from step: clashes and the crew list follow it. It and dekit set the shortest tight turn. It also decides when a LATE SHOW crew-rest ring turns from dashed to solid.
A man counts as busy until dekit. It and step set the shortest tight turn.
Ends a flyer's day: tomorrow's crew rest, the long day, OIL and Insights hours count to here, and so does the flight debrief advisory.
A shorter gap from landing to the next take-off is a tight turn. It is never less than dekit plus step.
What "+ In-time / Rally" writes after the time.
The brief before an EP sim, unless its remarks name one.
The debrief after a sim.
How long an AMT debrief runs when its DEBRIEF row has no end.
Rows with no end time
A sim with a start and no end is taken to run this long, for clashes and the crew list. It earns no OIL until its end is typed.
The same for a ground, programme or duty row.
Standby (SC, AVALON, BB)
A shift wholly inside it needs SC DAY; one reaching outside it needs SC NIGHT.
What an SC MAIN man's clash with each shows: a red warning or an amber advisory.
14 days before the week starts ›
An input last changed after it wears LATE.
the Wednesday two weeks before ›
The same for SANS availability.
Members file for others
A member may file a duty or commitment for someone else. Never leave, medical or SANS availability.
Full day of OIL
Weekend or holiday work this long or longer earns a full day; less earns a half.
Track Blue and Red sorties
Splits Insights' flying bars into Blue and Red, and asks Blue or Red under a formation.
Warning: Crew rest (<12h)
For a flying member: at least 12h (Crew rest) from the end of his day before to his earliest in-time, or to anything earlier that day.
Rest runs from the end of the day before to the first thing today: his in-time, his B where no in-time is typed, or anything earlier, such as a meeting.
The day before ends at its last commitment of any kind. A flight ends at landing plus the debrief ( ); anything else at its written end.
An input counts only if it is a duty or commitment, other than Personal or SANS Availability, with typed times.
Exactly is legal. A day with no flying asks for no rest.
A LATE SHOW remark keeps the warning. The ring is dashed while rest still clears by step, solid after.
Monday checks last Sunday. A Sunday that breaks Monday shows a "Breaks Monday" box.
A flying line with no times yet is not measured, but a typed brief, in-time or landing on it still counts.
An SC SPARE carries no crew rest either way, and a shift's start is its report.
Advisory: Tight turning — crew rest
His rest would be short if he reported the usual 3h before take-off (Report before take-off), but his typed in-time is later, so it clears.
Warning: No break day — too many days in a row
On the programme more than 6 days in a row.
Any tasking counts: a flight, a duty, a sim, a ground or programme row.
Leave or a downchit resets the count.
It counts last week's tail, and the warning lands on the day to clear.
Note: Long work day
More than 12h from first commitment to last.
Two things at once
Warning: Conflict — two events at once
Two commitments overlap for one man. Touching end to end is not a clash.
Advisory: On shift — also down for a ground event
An SC MAIN man is also down for something set to Advisory under SC MAIN clashes. A commitment input across the shift is red; a meeting stays amber.
A ground or programme item marked ⓘ is printed but never checked, and earns no OIL.
A row whose end reads earlier than its start runs into the next day.
An ordinary flying wave — it counts toward the day’s flying tally, and every line is fully cross-checked.
Warning: In-time / Rally — timings out of order
In-time, rally, brief, take-off and landing are not in that order.
The order is in-time, rally, brief, take-off, landing. Equal times are fine.
The B on the line is what is checked. A blank B is checked as the suggested brief, take-off less .
Out of order is red, but it never stops a day being published.
On an In-time / Rally line the first clock is used (09:00H or 0900). Write IN TIME, RALLY or both.
A formation's name makes the line that formation's; otherwise it is the whole wave's.
A clock later than take-off means the day before.
RALLY AFTER IN TIME, with no clock, means rally at that formation's in-time.
Advisory: In-time / Rally — check the reporting instruction
The app cannot read an In-time / Rally line, or RALLY AFTER IN TIME has no in-time.
Advisory: No time for the flight brief
Something sits between the brief and take-off. A blank B counts as the suggested one (Brief before take-off).
Advisory: No time for the flight debrief
Something sits inside landing plus 2h (Debrief after landing).
Less than 2h from landing to the next take-off (Tight turn, or Dekit plus Step if longer).
Two or more sorties in one day. One line names everyone; it is routine, not an error.
Advisory: Flight times — take-off and landing are the same
A line's take-off and landing are the same time. A flying line still earns its OIL; a standby shift earns none.
Advisory: No time for the sim brief
Something sits inside an EP sim's 15 min brief (EP sim brief), or an AMT's BRIEF row.
Advisory: No time for the sim debrief
Something sits inside a sim's 30 min debrief (Sim debrief), or an AMT's DEBRIEF row (AMT debrief, where that row has no end).
Warning: Qualification — illegal seat
A man in a seat he may not hold, such as a WSO in the front seat. Any pilot may fly the rear seat.
Warning: Illegal aircrew combination
An OCU pilot with a CAT A–D WSO, or the reverse. An instructor in either seat clears it.
Advisory: Crew solo — only allowed under syllabus
An OCU pilot with an OCU WSO. Allowed only on sorties the syllabus names.
Advisory: Crew combination — CO approval required
A CAT D pilot with a CAT C WSO, a CAT C pilot with a CAT D WSO, or two CAT Ds. The crew needs the CO's approval.
Advisory: OCU without IP
An OCU formation with no instructor (IW, IP, IR or FI).
Advisory: Incentive passenger — crew pairing needs approval
Ground crew in a rear seat. The ride needs approval. Ground crew are checked only for clashes, the long day and days in a row.
Warning: IRT without an IR examiner
IRT in the mission needs an IR in the formation; IRT in an aircraft's remarks needs one in that aircraft.
Warning: AAR currency — not qualified
AAR in the remarks needs the front seat's currency: night on a night wave, day otherwise. NAAR or DAAR says it outright.
Warning: AAR — back seat not cleared to instruct

A pilot not current may fly AAR as training only with an instructor in the back seat marked I for it on Quals (an I in place of the tick on DAAR or NAAR). That clears the front seat's currency warning; an instructor without the mark is flagged instead.
Warning: SC currency — wrong shift
A standby shift wholly inside 07:00 to 19:00 (SC day window) needs SC DAY; one reaching outside it needs SC NIGHT. A SPARE is checked the same as a MAIN.
Note: Night after day
NAAR needs DAAR, and SC NIGHT needs SC DAY. On Quals, removing the day one removes the night one.

A SPARE line is only checked for overseas / medically down, SC currency, a pilots-only front seat and not holding another SC seat or SC desk in the same hours — nothing else. A MAIN line is checked in full. Add as many of each as you need.

Overnight. Every line — MAIN or SPARE — is only checked for overseas / medically down, SC NIGHT currency, a pilots-only front seat and not holding another AVALON seat or the AVALON desk in the same hours. Nothing else. Add as many as you need.

Times are yours to set. The same checks as AVALON — overseas / medically down, SC currency for the hours typed, a pilots-only front seat and not holding another seat or the BB desk in the same hours. Nothing else. Add as many as you need.
Note: A shift's hours
A standby shift takes exactly its written hours: no step, dekit, brief or debrief.
Advisory: In-time window cut — busy between report and shift start
A typed B on an SC MAIN is the crew's in-time, and something sits between it and the shift start. It also starts his crew rest, his long day and his OIL from that time. A SPARE's B does nothing.
Note: Arming an SC seat
The crew list judges each man against that shift's hours only.
Leave, downchits and inputs
Note: An input closes its hours
Every input closes the man for the hours it covers, from the moment it is filed. One a scheduler has taken off the programme closes nothing.
Warning: On leave + flying
A man on leave is planned for a flight, sim, duty or ground slot.
A medically down man is planned. On ATT B he may still stand a duty, sim or ground slot, but not fly.
Warning: Personal input clash
Any other input clashes with a planned slot: a course, a meeting, an appointment, overseas duty.
Note: A seat with no times
Still checked against an absence covering the whole day; a part-day absence waits until the seat has times.

Leave and medical can be AM (to 12:00), PM (from 12:01) or all day, and a half day closes only its own half. A sortie counts from its step (Step before take-off), so AM leave still clashes with a wave that steps before noon.
Note: Standing SC SPARE
A man on local leave may still stand SC SPARE. Overseas leave or duty (OL, OD) or a medical code (HL, OML, ATT C, ATT B) may not: that is a warning.
Advisory: SANS availability — planned outside the availability filed
A SANS man planned outside the event or the hours he filed. Filing nothing raises nothing.
An input last changed after its cut-off (Inputs late cut-off) wears LATE: a mark, never a warning. Downchits never do.
Note: Weekend and holiday work earns OIL
Work on a weekend or public holiday earns OIL once the day is published: a full day or a half, by Full day of OIL.
Weekend or holiday work earns OIL once the day is published.
A man's day runs from his first report to his last end, gaps included: or more is a full day (FO), less is a half (HO).
A flight runs from its in-time (or Report before take-off, where none is typed) to landing plus the debrief.
A row with no times, or no end time, earns nothing. An Off day earns nothing.
SC SPARE, AVALON and BB earn only if switched on in OIL Earn.
A Duty & commitments input earns once its OIL question is answered yes.
A published day keeps its OIL until it is published again.
Warning: No OIL earned — a row has no usable times
On a weekend or holiday, a row with someone on it and no usable times earns nobody on it any OIL. The warning names the row.
Advisory: OIL waiting — this day is not published
A weekend or holiday with someone to earn is not published yet. Nobody earns until it is.
Advisory: No OIL — no Leave War period covers this date
No Leave War period covers this weekend or holiday, so its work earns nobody OIL. The day offers to create the period, before and after it is published.
Advisory: Became a holiday after publishing — republish for its OIL
A day published as a working day that the Leave War now calls a public holiday earns nothing until it is published again.
Advisory: No longer a holiday — republish to withdraw its OIL
A day published as a holiday that the Leave War no longer calls one keeps its OIL until it is published again, which withdraws it.
Advisory: Published before these seats counted — republish to credit them
A weekend or holiday published before the app counted an ALL AVAIL on a duty desk, sim or extra people line shows a pending change. Publish it again and the men behind that puck get their OIL.

Two things at once

Out of order is red, but it never stops a day being published.
On an In-time / Rally line the first clock is used (09:00H or 0900). Write IN TIME, RALLY or both.
A formation's name makes the line that formation's; otherwise it is the whole wave's.

Something sits between the brief and take-off. A blank B counts as the suggested one (Brief before take-off).
Advisory: No time for the flight debrief
Something sits inside landing plus 2h (Debrief after landing).
Less than 2h from landing to the next take-off (Tight turn, or Dekit plus Step if longer).
Two or more sorties in one day. One line names everyone; it is routine, not an error.

A line's take-off and landing are the same time. A flying line still earns its OIL; a standby shift earns none.

Something sits inside an EP sim's 15 min brief (EP sim brief), or an AMT's BRIEF row.

A man in a seat he may not hold, such as a WSO in the front seat. Any pilot may fly the rear seat.

An OCU pilot with a CAT A–D WSO, or the reverse. An instructor in either seat clears it.
Advisory: Crew solo — only allowed under syllabus
An OCU pilot with an OCU WSO. Allowed only on sorties the syllabus names.

A CAT D pilot with a CAT C WSO, a CAT C pilot with a CAT D WSO, or two CAT Ds. The crew needs the CO's approval.
Advisory: OCU without IP
An OCU formation with no instructor (IW, IP, IR or FI).

IRT in the mission needs an IR in the formation; IRT in an aircraft's remarks needs one in that aircraft.
